extracted: wave-7 opener, 2026-09-27, from runtime/dsh/host/dsh_runtime_host.c (JS_NewCFunction registrations in dsh_bind_globals, plus the JS_NewCFunctionData loader-internal and the __DSH_RELEASE__ flag) — signatures and semantics from the C comments and bodies
threadRule: All intrinsics run on the ONE serial runtime thread (ARCHITECTURE §6 / D2). The subprocess and sqlite seams own OS resources but never a second JS thread: subprocess bytes cross as base64 chunks the JS shim pumps over the ordinary timer seam; sqlite rows cross as plain objects.

intrinsics.name: __DSH_LOG_SINK__
intrinsics.semantics: The unified-log sink: the host emits the canonical `dsh.runtime.log: <jsonLine>` E2E line through the embedder's log sink. The ONLY logging exit; the harness also posts structured failure/debug rows through it (DSH_R3E_DEBUG=1).

intrinsics.name: __dshBusPost
intrinsics.semantics: JS -> host bus post: one JSON line handed to the embedder's bus sink (the web-boot carrier channel).

intrinsics.name: __dshEngineInfo
intrinsics.semantics: Engine identity probe (quickjs-ng 0.17.0 in this build).

intrinsics.name: __dshGatewayNegotiate
intrinsics.semantics: Gateway protocol negotiation: true only for 'gateway@1'; a rejection names the requested version in the host error.

intrinsics.name: __dshGatewayCall
intrinsics.since: pre-wave (real bridge replaced M1's canned responses)
intrinsics.semantics: The gateway bridge: assigns a monotonic call_id, parks the promise capability, and hands (call_id, name, args_json) to the embedder SYNCHRONOUSLY — the embedder hops the work off the runtime thread. MULTIPLE CALLS MAY BE IN FLIGHT. The embedder settles through dsh_runtime_gateway_settle and streams events through dsh_runtime_gateway_event (RUNTIME-THREAD-ONLY). The host no longer invents gateway results. Unknown/already-settled call ids fail loud at the settle call site.

intrinsics.name: __dshGatewayAbort
intrinsics.semantics: No promise of its own: the embedder matches the in-flight call (by the callId inside args_json) and cancels it. Dispatches as name='httpFetch.abort', args='{"callId":N}'.

intrinsics.name: __dshGatewayDescriptor
intrinsics.semantics: The stored gateway descriptor JSON verbatim, or the string 'null' when never set.

intrinsics.name: __dshLaunchEnv
intrinsics.semantics: The stored launch-env JSON object verbatim, or '{}'. The harness reads DSH_R3E_DEBUG from it; the suite driver reads DSH_* pins.

intrinsics.name: __dshComplete
intrinsics.semantics: Scenario completion: marks the run complete; anything falsy = fail (JS_ToBool; -1 on exception counts as fail).

intrinsics.name: __dshBundleRequire
intrinsics.semantics: The node:module seam's file read. `base` is the importing module's name (a bare specifier resolved through the SAME bare map the loader owns — one mapping surface, no second map to drift — or a bundle-root-relative path); `request` a relative path from its directory. ONLY package-style reads are served: .json and .js/.cjs/.mjs TEXT (the host returns raw bytes and owns NO module semantics — the shim layer's userland CJS loader evaluates CJS packages staged under vendor/). Everything else fails loud; escapes from the bundle root fail loud. Consumers: the CJS chains' db.json read, the pi-ai JSON seam.

intrinsics.name: __dshModuleDefine
intrinsics.semantics: Register a runtime-defined module under a specifier so import(specifier) resolves to it. Checked BEFORE the bare map (dsh_module_loader's documented order), so a registration both adds node: builtins the SHIMS table lacks and SHADOWS a broken vendored-probe resolution. REPLAY SEMANTICS: a second define REPLACES the source (npm-bridges/pi-ai duplicate rows rely on this). Query-buster interplay: the table keys by the QUERY-LESS name but the module compiles under the full query-bearing name, so every distinct query re-evaluates the current source exactly like node re-reading the file (the typert generator's loadSchema busts with '?test=<ts>-<n>').

intrinsics.name: btoa
intrinsics.semantics: Web-standard name, host-provided: base64 of a LATIN-1 string. JS_ToCStringLen hands back UTF-8, so the C decodes the UTF-8 back to char codes 0..255 (1-byte sequences cover 0x00..0x7F, 2-byte 0x80..0xFF); anything wider is a caller contract violation and fails loud ('btoa input must be latin-1').

intrinsics.name: atob
intrinsics.semantics: base64 -> LATIN-1 string: charCodeAt(i) == decoded byte i. JS_NewStringLen interprets input as UTF-8, so the raw bytes are RE-ENCODED as UTF-8 (each byte 0x80..0xFF becomes one 2-byte sequence) — feeding raw bytes mangled every high byte (measured: the zlib shim's b64ToBytes read a zstd frame's 0xB5 magic back as 0xFD; ASCII-only callers could never see it). Malformed base64 (bad char or padding after payload) fails loud.

intrinsics.name: getRandomValues
intrinsics.semantics: Web-standard name: fills the array in place from the platform RNG (arc4random_buf / getentropy / deterministic LCG fallback on hosts with no platform RNG — dsh-only, real hosts replace it) and returns it. Not cryptographically contracted beyond the platform RNG.

intrinsics.name: __zstdCompressB64
intrinsics.semantics: base64 in, base64 out. level defaults to 3 (the `level || 3` intrinsic contract; 0/absent -> 3). Errors surface as a JS Error whose message starts 'zstd: ' + the zstd error name (Agent B's shim codes against the prefix).

intrinsics.name: __zstdDecompressB64
intrinsics.semantics: base64 in, base64 out. Frame content size known AND within maxOutputBytes (0/omitted = unlimited) -> exact allocation; everything else (unknown size — streaming frames — or a hint above the cap) -> grow loop: start 256 KB, double, never exceed 256 MB. dstSizeTooSmall is the only retriable error; anything else fails loud with the 'zstd: ' prefix.

intrinsics.name: __dshProcSpawn
intrinsics.signature: ({command: string, args?: string[], cwd?: string, env?: object, stdio?: string|Array<string>, detached?: boolean}) -> {pid: number} | {error: {code: string, errno: number, message: 'spawn failed'}}
intrinsics.semantics: Portable POSIX fork/exec (fork/execvp via a PATH-walking execvpe over the CHILD-PROCESS envp — node's contract, not the parent's environ; poll/waitpid): the HOST owns the OS processes, children never execute JS (D2). stdio dispositions per fd: 'pipe' (0), 'ignore' -> /dev/null, 'inherit' -> the dsh's own fd; node's stdio array may name fds beyond 2 (fds 3..7 as DUPLEX socketpairs — libuv's shape, the ptc control channel rides fd 7; W6-U). Parent pipe ends are O_NONBLOCK (a paused reader must not deadlock the runtime — the 2MB didOpen abort test). exec (or chdir) failure surfaces node-shaped as {error:{code:'ENOENT',...}} with NO child to track; a missing workdir FAILS ENOENT with no child run (node's contract — the child-side mkdir that materialized every workdir broke it, measured 2026-09-27). Absolute argv entries (never argv[0]) that do not exist AS SPELLED but exist under the real bundle root are re-rooted there (node-faithful argv for the bundle-relative URL face, W5-R). Process table: 64 slots; a full table kills the fresh child and fails loud.

intrinsics.name: __dshProcSpawnSync
intrinsics.signature: ({command, args?, cwd?, env?, stdio?, input?: b64string, timeoutMs?: number}) -> {pid, status: number|null, signal: number|null, stdout: string, stderr: string, timedOut: boolean} | {error: {code, errno, message}, status: null, signal: null, stdout: '', stderr: '', pid: null}
intrinsics.semantics: Node's spawnSync result face. BLOCKS the runtime exactly like node blocks its event loop. input (b64) rides stdin then EOF; capture pipes drain to EOF poll-driven so either order works; timeoutMs (0/absent = none) SIGKILLs and reports timedOut. Unspawnable commands return {status: null, error} and do NOT throw (the pwsh/systemd-run probes test capability at module scope through this shape). Default encoding utf8 -> strings (buffer only when asked by the shim layer).

intrinsics.name: __dshProcPoll
intrinsics.signature: (pid: number) -> {out: b64|null, err: b64|null, outEof: boolean, errEof: boolean, exited: boolean, exitCode: number|null, signal: number|null, pendingStdin: number, flushError: number|null, extraOut: b64|null[5], extraEof: boolean[5], extraPending: number[5]}
intrinsics.semantics: The JS-side per-child pump contract: ONE poll = one non-blocking read pass + a WNOHANG reap. Flushes the stdin backpressure buffer first (whatever the child's pipe accepts this tick drains toward the reader; EPIPE surfaces as flushError so the JS shim fails the pending writes), then the extra channels' write buffers (W6-U). Drains stdout/stderr and the extra duplex channels; exitCode is null until a reaped-exit (WEXITSTATUS form); signal carries the terminating signal number. A RELEASED slot (settled + drained before the last JS pump tick) reports a settled child {out:null, err:null, outEof:true, errEof:true, exited:true, exitCode:0, signal:null} instead of throwing through a timer. Slot release: exited + all pipes EOF-closed + no pending bytes.

intrinsics.name: __dshProcWrite
intrinsics.signature: (pid: number, b64: string) -> {written: number} | {error: {code: string, errno: number}}
intrinsics.semantics: Write to the child's stdin. A dead stdin (never piped, closed, or EPIPE) returns {error:{code:'EPIPE', errno}}; partial writes leave the rest in the C-side backpressure buffer (flushed by the poll tick); a hard write error closes stdin and reports the errno name.

intrinsics.name: __dshProcEndStdin
intrinsics.semantics: Close the child's stdin (the EOF marker).

intrinsics.name: __dshProcWriteFd
intrinsics.signature: (pid: number, slot: number, b64: string) -> {written: number, buffered: number} | {error: {code, errno}}
intrinsics.semantics: The extra-channel write face: slot 0..4 maps to child fd 3..7. The socketpair is non-blocking; refused bytes buffer C-side (flushed by the poll tick) and `buffered` tells the JS shim to hold its write callback — the exact contract the stdin face honors. Slot out of range or a dead channel: TypeError / EPIPE.

intrinsics.name: __dshProcEndFd
intrinsics.semantics: Half-close the extra channel (shutdown SHUT_WR): the child reads EOF on its fd while our read side stays live — shutdown, not close.

intrinsics.name: __dshProcKill
intrinsics.semantics: The ESRCH contract of process.kill: a failed kill THROWS (TypeError naming the errno). Signal 0 probes existence without signalling. Signal names ('SIGTERM') or numbers; the table carries the 16 standard signals. detached children are setsid'd group leaders — never SIGKILLed at teardown (that is the embedder's teardown rule, not this call's).

intrinsics.name: __dshProcFacts
intrinsics.signature: () -> {nodePath: string|null, execPath: string|null, path: string|null, bundleRoot: string|null}
intrinsics.semantics: nodePath: a PATH search for an executable `node` (NULL when absent) — the suite leg pins process.execPath to it: the upstream contract spawns `process.execPath fixture.ts` expecting node's erasable-TS support. execPath: the running CLI, best effort (/proc/self/exe or _NSGetExecutablePath). path: $PATH. bundleRoot (W6-U): the REAL absolute path the loader's bundle-relative specifier space is rooted at (realpath of the CLI base, cached once) — the flat transpiled specs re-derive vendored-tree file paths through it (the __dshFlatPathMap builder), the same re-rooting __dshProcSpawn does for child argv.

intrinsics.name: __dshProcReadReal
intrinsics.semantics: One REAL file read for the parent side of the subprocess seam (children write marker files the runtime's VFS cannot see). NULL on any failure to open/stat. Size-capped at 16 MB — markers are tiny.

intrinsics.name: __dshProcMkdirReal
intrinsics.semantics: Recursive real-disk mkdir -p (0755). The workspace VFS mirrors the (real) profile container in memory only; directories the parent creates so a CHILD can write into them must materialize on the disk the child reads. The JS callers keep VFS behavior and add this write-through (best-effort).

intrinsics.name: __dshProcWriteFileReal
intrinsics.signature: (path: string, b64: string) -> {written: number} | {error: {code: string, errno: number}}
intrinsics.semantics: A REAL file write for the parent side of the seam: a SPAWNED child reads the real disk, so files the parent writes under the real-mirrored profile container must materialize there — the write-through twin of __dshProcMkdirReal (parents mkdir -p'd first, idempotent). 8 MB cap: a runaway mirror should fail loudly, not eat memory. Bad base64: TypeError.

intrinsics.name: __dshProcRmReal
intrinsics.semantics: A REAL unlink for the mirror: when the runtime's VFS rm removes a file the children could read, the real copy must go too or a subsequent child sees a zombie file. Files unlink directly; directories walk children depth-first (rm -rf for the recursive flag, rmdir-only otherwise — mirroring node's rm faces). ENOENT counts as success.

intrinsics.name: __dshProcChmodReal
intrinsics.semantics: chmod(2) over the real mirror: a hook script the runtime chmods +x in the VFS must land executable on the disk the seam's children read, or bash refuses it ('Permission denied', measured on the hooks bridge spec). Best-effort boolean: the VFS is the world of record; this only feeds the seam's children.

intrinsics.name: __dshProcStatReal
intrinsics.signature: (path: string) -> {mode: number, size: number, mtimeMs: number, isFile: boolean, isDirectory: boolean} | null
intrinsics.semantics: A REAL stat(2) probe. The runtime's fs faces are (partly) virtual; the subprocess seam's consumers (the vendored pre-spawn executability check) stat REAL binaries (the node running the fixture servers). VFS-first precedence lives in the JS callers — this is the FALLBACK only. NULL when stat fails.

intrinsics.name: __dshProcAccessReal
intrinsics.semantics: access(2): X_OK=1, R_OK=4 (the caller spells the mode bits).

intrinsics.name: __dshSqliteOpen
intrinsics.semantics: Open (create) a REAL sqlite database (SQLITE_OPEN_READWRITE|CREATE; engine = the ALREADY-LINKED system sqlite3, the iSH userland depends on it). node:sqlite's documented default is files 0600 with the -wal/-journal sidecars inheriting — enforced by chmod at CREATION only (an existing-but-empty medium counts as created; reopening never overrides the caller's own chmods; re-enforced after every write because sidecars materialize lazily — extended result codes on). 16 db slots; table-full runs ONE GC pass (handles are GC-owned: their native allocations put no pressure on the JS GC) then re-scans; still-full fails loud 'node:sqlite: database table full (16)'.

intrinsics.name: __dshSqliteClose
intrinsics.semantics: Explicit close: finalizes every statement of the db first (detaching still-live JS StatementSync objects — their finalizers later see NULL and only free), then sqlite3_close. Unknown handle: TypeError.

intrinsics.name: __dshSqliteExec
intrinsics.semantics: sqlite3_exec; failure throws InternalError 'node:sqlite: exec: <engine message>'. Re-enforces the 0600 mode after (sidecars).

intrinsics.name: __dshSqlitePrepare
intrinsics.semantics: sqlite3_prepare_v2; failure throws 'node:sqlite: prepare: ...'. 128 stmt slots with the same GC-collect-and-retry as open (W6-V: the 128-slot table exhausted mid-suite on unclosed ad-hoc statements — node GC-finalizes, the vendored session-search prepares per query).

intrinsics.name: __dshSqliteRun
intrinsics.semantics: Bind + step once (SQLITE_DONE or ROW ok), then reset. Binding: reset + clear_bindings first; undefined/null params = none; array = positional from 1; object = NAMED (':k', then '@k', then '$k' — node's named-parameter spellings, first match wins per key). Values bind as null/number/string/blob (bools as 0/1; integral doubles as int64; typed arrays as blob; anything else SQLITE_MISMATCH).

intrinsics.name: __dshSqliteGet
intrinsics.semantics: Bind + step; SQLITE_ROW -> the row object (column-name keys, later duplicates: last wins — node's shape; values as null/number/string/Uint8Array); SQLITE_DONE -> null (the JS shim maps null -> undefined — node:sqlite's get() returns UNDEFINED for no row; the C null read as a present-but-null row crashed rowHeader, W6-V); else throw.

intrinsics.name: __dshSqliteAll
intrinsics.semantics: Bind ONCE, then step to exhaustion — re-binding inside the loop resets the statement and restarts the query, so every iteration re-yielded row 1 and the drain never reached SQLITE_DONE (W6-V: the session-query search walk hung forever on the first result set). Non-DONE end: throw.

intrinsics.name: __DSH_RELEASE__
intrinsics.semantics: Injected at context-bind time ONLY when the host compiles with -DDSH_RELEASE (the platforms' Release configurations): the JS logger's debug/info become no-ops while each embedded logger.js stays byte-identical to the canonical checkout (no second source to drift). Debug builds leave the global absent, which the logger treats as 'not release'.

intrinsics.name: __dshImportMetaResolve
intrinsics.signature: (specifier: string) -> string — NOT a global: JS_NewCFunctionData closure held by the loader
intrinsics.semantics: The import.meta.resolve implementation: one C function serves every module via JS_NewCFunctionData (the func_data dups the importing module's name). Loader-internal — registered as a property of import.meta, never on globalThis.

notes: 39 JS_NewCFunction registrations in dsh_bind_globals (including the web-named btoa/atob/getRandomValues); __DSH_RELEASE__ is a JS_SetPropertyStr boolean; __dshImportMetaResolve is a JS_NewCFunctionData closure owned by the loader (no global binding).
The zstd intrinsics' error convention: a JS Error whose message starts 'zstd: ' + the zstd error name — the node:zlib shim codes against the prefix.
The subprocess seam compiles portable POSIX only (fork/execvp/poll/waitpid/socketpair): it builds on the mobile hosts but only the dsh JS ever calls it.

sqlite binding matrix: bind null/undefined->NULL, bool->0/1, number->int64 (integral) or double, string->text, typed array->blob; reads return null/number/string/Uint8Array — the node:sqlite defaults the vendored schemas rely on.
